May we research the stress of time? Time was always measured relative to something. Relative to the sun, the season.

But today, time is measured by a precise floating point value. A number indicates next-to-nothing

Not to mention the very real physiological health issues by the problem of time; sleep,

It is actually one of the hardest parts of modern life; balance (almost entirely in our control, assuming we allocate time and resources properly.) Balancing the Domains in one's life (i.e., Social, Work, Community, Leisure, Health, etc. This is somewhat in our control) according to Time (not in our control) according to our perception (In our influential control). From Ultradian Cycles, to the Circadian-Rhythm, our natural time-keeping mechanisms are relative-to-one-another; not to a central time-keeping maestro. The actual Sycnrhony of the Neurological Symphony can be structurally described as: Cluster-based-Hierarchies (much like natural Human organization.) One group influences another group, and those groups form larger groups. It's Cybernetic in essence; with no source arbiter of control; the control itself is a dynamic of feedback and correction/regulation.

Coming back to the stress of time; it is as if a person who is not perfect; they will undoubtedly fall out of order. Here is where the local research comes in; what is a person supposed to do, when their natural physiology is already depleted and exhausted? How is such a person meant to be reponsible? Are most people running on constant short? What is causing this epidemic? What is one to do? When a person wants to be a reponsible citizen and member, but cannot afford to collapse

Materialistic correction: I argue we are not merely our Physiology; and given enough reason or resource, we can push our bodies beyond what once

Here is a sample scenario: Person A wakes up early, at 4:00 AM. Person B wakes up late in the morning, at 11:00 AM. Despite nearly 6 hours of difference, both persons (assuming this is their natural wake up schedule) are running on their own internal Circadian-Rhythm. The clock essentially "defines" their kind of person. "Person A is reponsible, and Person B is irresponsible." Person B looks at the clock "It is 4:00, I have enough time for Decision A." Person A goes grocery shopping, and even has time at the end of the day for leisure and socializing. While Person B is struggling through even the most basic of chores; not even mentioning work or socializing; there's simply no time or energy left in the person.

Now; this is not to justify "a wreckless, YOLO lifestyle. No time, no stress." Becuase according to Systems theory; time sets the order of synchronization in systems. Without time, many sophisticated systems fall apart (this is why Einstein's General Relativity was so important in today's world.) However, one cannot simply "force Person B to live a perfect life in the Industrial Age." Arguably, Person B is oriented to a proto-industrial age.

However, this is where I propose a radical "Post-Industrial" order of keeping time: Proportionality over Precision. We have previously researched this; replacing integers with proportions "it's half-past noon" over "it is 12:30 PM."

No system is 100% energy or resource efficient; it is madness to attempt to redefine our natural time-keeping systems by a machine with perfect precision; a clockwork of absolute order. There must be an Equillibria; a balance between precision and open-ness.

Here is what the industrial age and the clock do not consider; Person A has a healthy (enough) nervous system to Person B is in a chronic state of constant energy deficit.

By the end of the day, Person B feels depleted, exhausted and ends up staying awake at night due to trouble sleeping.

Anyone with any Humanitarian sense would atleast see the implied "unfairness of time rushing."
